WEEKLY DISCUSSION: Is Reddit now doomed to be a complete failure?

Every site is doomed to failure, the question is not if, but when. People are making this out to be the downfall of reddit, but I doubt it. The very large majority of reddit frankly don't care. I read somewhere that only like 1% (?) was "revolting". This is not the end for reddit, but rather the rise of it's competitors.

Seconded. Not a complete failure. There is too much momentum behind the site to just come to a complete stop on the current hiccups.

I don't think that it will go down in flames, despite all the salty attitudes right now. The hivemind constituents will fare just fine, as will the casual users who don't really care to engage in the petty infighting, continuing to play the game as they have for years, and likely stay for further bumbling monetization attempts / idiotic corporate decisions. Those not interested in being subject to downvote brigade for having a different opinion, or censorship to maintain political "correctness", or frustrated with the overall direction (and principled enough to just walk) will leave: This is a relatively small portion of Reddit's population.

(As a sidenote, I am really encouraged by the things I see on Voat, because it's none of the problems mentioned above, and am super happy to be here. The smaller community, merit-based voting, and less-quantity-but-higher-quality almost no shitposts content reminds me of forums from days past and I am really digging it.)
It's going to fail, but it's going to be less "catastrophic implosion" and more "slowing to a crawl". If I remember correctly, that's how things went with digg.

I want to discuss the ways in which we can evolve this community to make it a unique place for people to visit!

 

The Reddit Situation

I realize that most of us are migrants from Reddit. I get it, Reddit got involved with corporate bullshit and shifted the culture of the site. Unfortunately Reddit did not know how to handle its fame in a better way, so it had to resort to corporate business tactics to stay afloat. as unfortunate as this may be, it is no reason to obsess over it. I understand many of you are angry at Reddit. I know I am. We need to focus that energy into making this a better community than Reddit rather than simply bash it all the time. How do we do that you ask?

 

Submit Content

Lets take a look at another popular user driven website: 4chan. The thing that makes 4chan intriguing is that most of the content revolves around text discussion rather than submitted links. There is a lot of power in making text posts. This is something that holds sites similar to Voat and Reddit back because it creates a barrier between users and posters. Many times super users generate 90% of the content on a site like this because they have a very good system to find content and post it via link post faster than the average user. If you take a closer look at a site like 4chan, you will find that many posts either have no link, or are discussing the link rather than simply (read lazily) posting it. This isn't a call to adopt 4chan's culture, but I think looking at this community as an example isn't a bad idea.

use upvoats wisely

Something that sets Voat apart is the limitations users have on voating. Something I see far too much of on the front page are reaction gifs. I understand that this is a very popular thing around these parts, but I feel people are throwing their precious voats away on something that isn't contributing all that much. The front page and /v/all is our first impression we have on new visitors so we need to make it count. I implore you to use your voating powers to upvoat relevant comments and quality posts.

 

That's all I got, hopefully we can make this place awesome!
